summary: Find the longest contiguous subarray in which the absolute difference between any two elements is at most limit.
mainInsight: The largest pairwise difference in a window is simply max - min, so a window is valid iff max - min <= limit. Track the window's max and min in O(1) with two monotonic deques while sliding.

approaches.name: Brute force
approaches.summary: Check every subarray's max and min.

approaches.name: Window + two heaps (lazy deletion)
approaches.summary: Max-heap and min-heap with stale-index removal.

approaches.name: Window + two monotonic deques
approaches.summary: A decreasing deque gives the max, an increasing deque the min; shrink while max - min > limit.
weaknesses: Two structures to keep in sync

personalSolution.notes: Optimal; the inline reasoning about max - min is exactly the key insight.

promptVariants: Which technique solves this problem, and what in the statement or constraints points to it?
Name the technique you would use here and the clue in the problem that tells you.
What approach fits this problem, and which part of the statement gives it away?
cards.answer: Sliding window with two monotonic deques that track the window's maximum and minimum. Clue: The largest pairwise difference in a subarray is its max minus its min, so a window is valid when that is at most the limit; slide a window and keep its max and min available as it moves.
keyPoints: The largest pairwise difference in a subarray is its max minus its min, so a window is valid when that is at most the limit; slide a window and keep its max and min available as it moves.
cards.explanation: Validity depends only on the window's extremes, which monotonic deques maintain in constant amortised time.

rubric.technique: Sliding window with two monotonic deques that track the window's maximum and minimum

alsoValid.name: Compute the max and min of every subarray

rubric.clue: The largest pairwise difference in a subarray is its max minus its min, so a window is valid when that is at most the limit; slide a window and keep its max and min available as it moves.

promptVariants: Which structure gives the window max and min in O(1) amortised?
What combination solves this problem in O(n)?
options: Sliding window with two monotonic deques
A single stack storing every window value
Prefix sums over the window's elements
Binary search on the limit for each window
cards.answer: Sliding window with two monotonic deques
cards.explanation: One deque tracks the maximum, the other the minimum of the current window.

incorrectOptionExplanations.A single stack storing every window valu: A stack cannot expire the oldest element.

promptVariants: Why is checking only max - min enough to validate the window?
Explain why every pair is within limit iff max - min <= limit.
cards.answer: The largest absolute difference between any two elements of a set is always between its maximum and minimum. So if that difference is <= limit, all pairs are; if it is greater, the pair (max, min) already violates it.
cards.explanation: That reduces a pairwise condition to two aggregates.

promptVariants: What do the two deques hold and how do you expire elements?
State the invariant of max_queue and min_queue.
cards.answer: They hold indices within the window: max_queue with decreasing values (front = window max), min_queue with increasing values (front = window min). When l advances, indices < l are popped from the fronts.
keyPoints: Expire by index from the front
cards.explanation: Same idea as Sliding Window Maximum, done twice.

promptVariants: Time complexity of the two-deque solution: ___
Each index enters and leaves each deque once, so the time is ___.
What is the space cost and when is it the worst?
How large can the deques get?
cards.answer: O(n) in the worst case: a strictly decreasing array fills max_queue with the whole window, a strictly increasing one fills min_queue.

promptVariants: Why does the shrink loop set `l = min(max_queue[0], min_queue[0]) + 1` and then purge both deques?
How does the shrink step restore validity?
cards.answer: The violation involves the current max and min; to fix it one of them must leave the window. The earlier of their indices must go first, so l jumps just past min(front indices); then expired indices are popped from both deques. Repeat until max - min <= limit.
keyPoints: Drop the earlier of the two extremes
Purge expired indices from both deques
cards.explanation: Moving l one step at a time would also work.

promptVariants: What is the answer for nums = [9,3,5,6,2,4], limit = 3?
cards.explanation: [3,5,6] has max 6 and min 3 (difference 3 <= 3); adding 9 on the left (difference 6) or 2 on the right (difference 4) breaks the limit.

incorrectOptionExplanations.2: A window of length 3 exists, so 2 is too small.
incorrectOptionExplanations.4: Every length-4 window has a max-min difference above 3.
incorrectOptionExplanations.6: The whole array has max 9 and min 2 (difference 7).
